name: ARGENTINA

flag.title: Sol de Mayo
flag.note: Blue & white bands; golden Sun of May

lead: Argentina stretches from steamy jungle in the north to icy Patagonia in the south. It has six climate zones. Thundering Iguazú Falls, giant glaciers, and the highest peak outside Asia are all here.
geo: Argentina is the eighth-largest country in the world. The Andes run along its whole western edge. The grassy Pampas in the east are perfect for cattle. Windy Patagonia in the far south has glaciers.
Iguazú Falls in the north has nearly 275 separate cascades. Ushuaia is the world's most southerly city. Cruise ships stop there before Antarctica.
animals: The capybara, Earth's biggest rodent, can weigh as much as a large dog. It paddles in the Iberá wetlands beside caimans. The giant anteater slurps up 35,000 ants a day.
Punta Tombo, in Patagonia, has the world's largest Magellanic penguin colony. Guanacos, wild relatives of the llama, roam the windy steppe.
culture: Tango was born in the port neighbourhoods of Buenos Aires in the 1880s. It blends African rhythms with European waltzes. Couples dance it on street corners every night.
The asado (barbecue) is almost a religion. Families grill beef for hours over wood embers. Mate, a bitter herbal tea, is sipped through a metal straw from a shared gourd.
history: Humans reached the tip of Patagonia about 13,000 years ago. The Inca pushed into the northwest in the 1400s. Spanish explorers arrived in 1516.
Argentina declared independence on 9 July 1816, a national holiday today. General José de San Martín then crossed the Andes to free Chile and Peru.
wows: Argentina made the world's first animated feature film, 'El Apóstol', in 1917.
Buenos Aires has more psychoanalysts per person than any other city.
Argentina's national sport, El Pato, is a horseback game mixing polo and basketball.
The first public radio broadcast came from a Buenos Aires rooftop in 1920.
Aconcagua, at 6,959 m, is the tallest peak in the Western and Southern Hemispheres.
A Titanosaur found in Patagonia may be the largest dinosaur ever found.
In 1978, the first Antarctic-born baby arrived at an Argentine base.

myths.myth: It snows at Christmas in Argentina
myths.fact: Seasons are flipped south of the equator. Christmas comes in summer, so families swim and picnic.
Some live on warm coasts. Penguins also live in South Africa and the Galápagos.
